title: I Got A Woman – song facts, recording info and more!
content:
The Beatles’ songs – complete A-Z list » I Got A Woman

Written by: Ray Charles
Recorded: 16 July 1963, 31 March 1964
Producer: Terry Henebery

Released: 30 November 1994 (UK), 5 December 1994 (US)

Available on:
Live At The BBC
On Air – Live At The BBC Volume 2

Contents

Toggle

Personnel

John Lennon: vocals, rhythm guitar
Paul McCartney: bass
George Harrison: lead guitar
Ringo Starr: drums

The Beatles recorded two versions of Ray Charles’ ‘I Got A Woman’ for BBC radio.

Charles released ‘I Got A Woman’ as a single in December 1954. The Beatles performed it live on many occasions in the early 1960s, prior to their record deal with EMI, with John Lennon on lead vocals.

Although the group never recorded it in the studio, they performed ‘I Got A Woman’ twice for BBC radio shows. Their arrangement was more similar to Elvis Presley’s 1956 version, which The Beatles most likely heard on his debut UK album Rock ‘N’ Roll No 1.

In the studio

The Beatles first recorded ‘I Got A Woman’ on 16 July 1963 at the BBC Paris Theatre in London, for the ninth edition of the Pop Go The Beatles programme. It was first broadcast on 13 August. This version can be heard on the Live At The BBC collection.

They performed it again on 31 March 1964 for Saturday Club. Recorded at the Playhouse Theatre, London, it first transmitted on 4 April that year, and officially released on the 2013 album On Air – Live At The BBC Volume 2.

This second version of ‘I Got A Woman’ was faster than the 1963 take. It featured a double-tracked vocal by John Lennon, but without the stop-start rhythms and the delayed appearance of the drums.
